newsitem.title: USA: Mayor's veto may delay Miami airport bond deal.
newsitem.headline: Mayor's veto may delay Miami airport bond deal.

text.p: Dade County, Fla., may have to postpone a $124 million airport revenue refunding bond issue because of the mayor's veto of the underwriting team, county Finance Director Rachel Baum said Friday.
The issue had been set for pricing at the end of April.

County Mayor Alex Penelas vetoed the selection of the team of underwriters on Friday, citing concerns about allegations of unethical conduct by Smith Barney Inc. The firm, a unit of the Travelers Group Inc, was to have been senior manager for the deal.

Penelas vetoed the selection because Smith Barney is under investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission in relation to a 1994 Dade County Water and Sewer Authority bond ofering in which Smith Barney and Howard Gary & Co servied as co-senior managers.
The investigation has focused on a savings presentation made to county officials and certain fees Smith Barney received in the transaction.
Smith Barney listed the investigation on disclosure documents that the county has recently begun asking underwriters for before each Dade deal.
The disclosure was discussed when the underwriting team was assembled, but county officials had long been aware of the probe, Baum said.
"Everyone in the county was aware of that issue," Baum said. "The issue was discussed and resolved. We didn't take it as a new development."
The county uses a standing pool of underwriting teams, assigning deals on a rotating basis, but often reconfigures the teams when a team member has a conflict.

The selection is made by the County Manager's Finance Committee and then sent to the Board of Commissioners for approval. The commission approved the team for the aviation deal by an 8-1 vote on Feb 25.
"The board was made aware of the Smith Barney controversy way back," Baum said.
Also chosen were Goldman Sachs & Co, Bear Stearns & Co Inc and Douglas James Securities Inc. Officials at those firms could not immediately be reached for comment.
Baum said she did not know whether the other firms would remain on the deal.
Penelas' veto announcement directed the county manager to reconfigure the team, and raised no complaints against the other firms.

It was the first time Penelas has used his mayoral veto, which was created when voters adopted a strong mayor form of government last year. He said the Smith Barney investigation created "a cloud" over the firm. The veto could be overturned by a two-thirds vote of the commission.

The county has excluded small, minority-owned firms -- including Howard Gary & Co, Grigsby & Associates and Guzman & Co -- from deals because of ethical concerns. Penelas said Smith Barney and other major Wall Street firms should be held to the same standards as those firms.

The $124 million bond issue is a forward delivery refunding transaction and would refund the aviation department's Series S and T bonds, which have coupons that range from 6.75 percent to 7.29 percent,
